title: ASR Research Profile (profiles/<name>.json)
description: A named, ordered selection of registries for one line of work (spec/11). A research profile says only WHERE to look: which registries, in what priority, optionally narrowed to some of each registry's own topics and facet values. It never restates or overrides anything a source profile owns (access, auth, limits, robots, routing), and it carries nothing about a client or a question. Not to be confused with a source profile (source.json, spec/02).

profile_id.description: Content-addressed: prf- + first 12 hex of sha256("prf\n" + name) (spec/06.1).

name.description: Slug; MUST equal the file's basename without .json.

contact.description: URL or mailto: for whoever maintains the profile. Registries keep their own contact for fetch User-Agents.

registries.description: In priority order: a consumer consults the first entry first and reports results grouped in this order.

path.description: Relative path from this profile file to the registry folder (the one holding registry.json). No absolute paths (spec/01.1 location independence).

registry_id.description: The registry's own id, as a check that the path still points at the intended registry (profile_registry_mismatch).

use.description: One line: what this registry is for within the profile.

topics.description: Optional narrowing to topic ids declared in THAT registry's topics.json (a topic's descendants are included). Absent = all topics.

facets.description: Optional default facet filter, {<facet-id>: [<value-id>...]}, using THAT registry's facets.json (facets are registry-local, spec/01.5). Same semantics as query --facet: AND across axes, OR within one. A caller's own --facet on the same axis replaces the default.
